data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A token-exhausted run can be safely resumed iff three conditions jointly hold: (1) clean halt\u2014the final event was fully committed and persisted before the exhaustion signal was raised, so no partial write exists at the log tail; (2) append-only identity integrity\u2014the hash chain (or equivalent identity structure) from genesis to the tail event is verifiable and unbroken; (3) resumption strictly appends new events after the verified tail without mutating, inserting, or reordering any existing event. Resumption must be refused when the tail is a partial or uncommitted write, when the chain is broken, or when any evidence suggests an interrupted commit.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Exhaustion is detected during a write, leaving a partial or torn event at the tail\u2014chain verification fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The commit of the last event succeeded on the writer but the persist to durable storage did not complete before the halt.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The chain is intact but the budget accountant's internal state is inconsistent with the log tail (e.g., budget was charged for an event that was never committed).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Resumption attempts to compact or rewrite the log tail to 'clean up' a partial event, mutating the append-only identity.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log is intact but the resuming process has a different code version whose event schema is incompatible with the existing chain.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Token-budget exhaustion is detected by the budget accountant, which signals halt. If the signal is checked at a safe point\u2014between event commits, not mid-write\u2014then the log tail is a complete, chain-linked event. On resumption, the system verifies the chain from genesis to tail (O(n) or O(log n) with MMR), reconstructs state via replay, and continues appending. The append-only identity is preserved because no existing event is touched; new events extend the chain from the last verified hash.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
